checks.label: Extreme values in the tails distort the mean but not the median, since the median is based on ranks: slipping the ringed reading off the top of the scale lifts the mean of the fifty by a fiftieth of the slip and moves the median by half a meter step at most, at every random error

The mean will be pulled in the direction of the skewness: if the right tail is heavier than the left, the mean will be greater than the median. Insulation resistance nudged by factors makes a bell about 200 MΩ on a scale of 20 columns a decade, each 12% more than the last; on an even scale its mean sits above its median and the settled beam balances there, level, with every reading on both scales and no bead under r 3.5

From every raw data value, subtract the mean, square the results, average them over one fewer than the count and then take the square root: every SD worked on screen follows that recipe line by line and agrees with the standard deviation of its readings

Worked by hand: 0.79, 0.80, 0.80, 0.81 and 0.85 Ω add to 4.05 Ω and balance at 0.81 Ω, with 0.04 Ω of distance each side; nine readings of 0.50 Ω and one of 1.50 Ω have a mean of 0.60 Ω and a median of 0.50 Ω; 0.77 to 0.82 Ω give squares adding to 0.0016, then 0.0004 and an SD of 0.02 Ω; 0.75 to 0.83 Ω give 0.0036, 0.0009 and 0.03 Ω; piles A and B both span 0.08 Ω with SDs of 0.028 and 0.040 Ω; the bumpy and flat piles 0.016 and 0.035 Ω; the ten circuits a mean of 0.62 Ω and an SD of 0.13 Ω

The rule on screen: twelve nudges of −½ to +½ add to an error of SD 1, within 2% over 20,000 simulated readings; halving the random error from 0.02 to 0.01 Ω takes the fifty from 10 columns to 5 and their tallest stack from 11 to 20 beads, nearly twice, with the mean within 0.002 Ω of 0.80 Ω both times

A slipped probe: with the ringed reading at 1.80 Ω, 1.00 Ω too high, the mean of the fifty is exactly 0.02 Ω higher and the SD jumps to about 0.14 Ω, at a random error of 0.02 Ω and of 0.01 Ω; honest, the SD comes out close to the random error

Drawn right: settled, the fulcrum sits exactly under the mean and the beam is level at every random error, honest or slipped; a slipped reading past the scale sits on its end column with an arrow, never clipped; no bead of the fifty is drawn smaller than r 3.5; each puzzle's fulcrum lands where its pick puts it

Each puzzle accepts only its right answer, and before an answer nothing in its picture gives it away: no fulcrum where the balance point is asked, no worked rows where the SD is asked, no SD brackets where spreads are compared, no rings on the far beads
Every demonstration has finished arriving within 4.5 s of its screen opening, none starting before the 0.35 s screen fade ends, and every answer's motion, and the switch of scale, within 2.5 s

warnings: K.sound is used but no K.button press played anything: play sound from a K.button's press so the self-test (and Dan) can reach it.
